cases.name: Cindy Winter
cases.about: She was a student at Canyon del Oro High School.
cases.narrative: On 3/23/1970, her partially nude body was found by a couple on horseback under a bush in a small gully near the Oro Valley County Club's golf course. The gully ran alongside a dirt road through the desert and it was an extension of Valle de Oro St. in Oro Valley Estates. She had a puncture wound at the base of her skull and several puncture wounds to her back. She was killed by three .22 bullets. She had been riding her bike to the country club and never arrived. He shot her in the back with a rifle as she rode her bike.

cases.name: Miguela "Lida" Burhans
cases.narrative:
He raped and killed her in her bedroom between 1:30 pm and 2:30 pm in the afternoon. He slashed her in the head, throat and breasts. She died from a combination of strangulation and two deep cuts to her throat that severed her carotid artery. It was determined the stab wounds were not instantaneously fatal and she would have been conscious for several minutes after the stabbing. Her husband found her body face down on their bedroom floor in a pool of blood, unclothed from the waist down. A knife sheath and blood stains were on the bed next to her body, and scattered throughout the bedroom were fragments of a broken clay table lamp that had previously sat on a nightstand. The electrical cord used to strangle her from the broken lamp was still around her neck and her hand was still intertwined in it, demonstrating that she had been conscious when Walden wrapped it around her neck and was struggling to loosen it. She had bruises and injuries on her arms, legs, and mouth, as well as scrapes on her neck and chest.

cases.name: Sachiko McClurg
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Sachiko was born July 26, 1952 in Tokyo, Japan to Miyuki Battles. Sachiko moved to the United States with her family when she was 16. She graduated school and helped raise her siblings. At 19, she met and married the love of her life. They worked to build a beautiful life together. They learned of Jesus and His saving grace, she knew she was loved by God and greater things were yet to come. Sachiko worked as a teacher at her kids' school and later became the senior manager at the credit union. She raised 3 great kids who became successful caring adults. She had 5 beautiful grandchildren that she loved deeply. She enjoyed flower gardens and grew flowers in every color. She loved her trips with her husband, exploring and learning about their family history. Sachiko was an amazing woman with a beautiful heart. She was a loving wife, mother, grandmother, sister and friend. She will be deeply missed."

cases.name: Mary Falo Ainuu
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Mary was the second oldest child of Fuauli T. and Mele V. Falo. She was born in Utulei, American Samoa and grew up in San Francisco, CA. She met her husband, Cheney, in Carson, CA and married him in 1985. Together, they had four daughters and adopted a son. Mary's faith in God motivated and guided her life. Serving in the Army Reserve, mentoring women and teaching Sunday School, and being a caregiver to her widowed mother are just a few examples of her service to God and others. Mary's legacy is her children. She devoted her life to raising, homeschooling, and caring for them.

Mary was the brightest, most beautiful light. She loved to laugh and have fun. She impacted everyone with her kindness, generosity, and humor. She always shared her faith and encouraged everyone to seek God. She is survived by her husband, children, siblings, and many nieces and nephews who will miss her dearly."
